title: I can do that!
grammar: can / can't for ability; Statements and yes/no questions; Degrees of ability
pair_game: Act out an ability. Your partner guesses: “You can swim!” Then swap!

grammar_box.title: can / can’t
grammar_box.tip: can + verb (no -s!): She can swim. NOT She can swims. (qila oladi)

questions: What can you do very well? Tell me about your best ability.
Can you play a musical instrument? Which one? How well?
What sport can you play? Are you very good at it?
What can't you do but really want to learn?
Can you cook? What dishes can you make?
Can you speak any other languages besides Uzbek and English?
What can your best friend do that you can't?
Can you draw or paint? Do you enjoy art?
What is something you couldn't do before but can do now?
What ability do you think is the most useful in everyday life?
starters: I can … very well. It’s my best ability!
Yes, I can play the … . I can play it … . / No, I can’t.
I can play … . I’m very good / OK at it.
I can’t … , but I really want to learn.
Yes, I can cook. I can make … . / No, I can’t cook.
Yes, I can speak … . / No, I can’t.
My best friend can … , but I can’t.
Yes, I can draw … . I enjoy art because … .
Before, I couldn’t … . Now I can … .
I think … is the most useful ability.
samples: What can you do very well? Tell me about your best ability.
I **can** play chess **very well**. I play with my grandpa every evening!
Can you cook? What dishes can you make?
Yes, I **can** cook a little. I **can** make eggs and tea. I **can’t** make plov.
What can your best friend do that you can't?
My best friend Ali **can** swim very fast. I **can’t** swim, but I want to learn.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: What can you do very well?

game.title: Find someone who…
game.rules: Walk around the class. Ask: “Can you …?” If the answer is “Yes, I can”, write a name.
items: … can sing a song in English.
… can play the dutar or piano.

mini_talk.title: My abilities
plan: Say what you can do well
Say what you want to learn
mini_talk.model: Hello! I’m Laylo. I **can** sing and dance **very well**. I **can** speak Uzbek, English and a little Russian. I **can** draw flowers. But I **can’t** swim, and I **can’t** play football. I want to learn to swim this summer. **Can** you swim?
